---
title: "Core Concepts"
---

MINTverse computes prevalence and clinical-case trajectories in two stages, an inversion in
`estimint` from a measured prevalence or biting rate to the EIR that would sustain it, followed
by a forward run of the campaign in `stateMINT`. The emulator covers six years, three before the
campaign and three after. Four quantities move through the pipeline, EIR, HBR, prevalence and
cases, and each is either an equilibrium value or a path through time. That distinction decides
which package produces it. A net mix and a pyrethroid resistance level are reduced to one
lethality number, `dn0`, before either stage will accept them. Both stages have a training
domain, and both enforce it silently. Nothing is fitted at call time.

::: {.chapter-outline}
- [The MINTverse pipeline](pipeline.qmd) — The two stages, `run_scenarios`, and the domain limits both packages enforce silently.
- [EIR, HBR, prevalence, and cases](equilibrium.qmd) — The four quantities, their units, and the difference between an equilibrium and a trajectory.
- [Interventions and nets](interventions.qmd) — The four net formulations, pyrethroid resistance, and `dn0`.
- [The models](models.qmd) — Three gradient-boosted trees in `estimint`, and one state-space emulator in `stateMINT`.
- [Accuracy and speed](validation.qmd) — The emulator against the simulator on held-out runs, and what a prediction costs.
:::
